title: Soft Body Collision Sculptor
description: Two shader balls float in a zero-gravity arena, each wrapped in a visible soft-body mesh that deforms on impact. The user launches one ball toward the other by dragging to set velocity, then adjusts stiffness, damping, and pressure parameters on each body independently, watching the deformation ripple across both surfaces as they collide and settle.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements an interactive soft-body collision scene. Load ShaderBall.glb and ShaderBall2.glb using GLTFLoader from a CDN. Position ShaderBall at (-3, 0, 0) and ShaderBall2 at (3, 0, 0). Wrap each loaded mesh in a soft-body simulation by duplicating its geometry into a spring-mass system: store vertex positions in a Float32Array, connect neighboring vertices with spring constraints, and update positions each frame using Verlet integration. Each soft body must have independent parameters: stiffness (0.1-1.0), damping (0.01-0.5), internal pressure (0.0-2.0). Provide an HTML panel with six sliders, three per ball, labeled clearly. Implement a drag-to-launch interaction: when the user clicks and drags on ShaderBall, draw a visible arrow helper showing the launch direction and magnitude, and on release apply that velocity to all vertices of ShaderBall's soft body. Detect collision between the two bodies using bounding-sphere overlap, then resolve vertex-level penetrations by pushing vertices apart along the contact normal and applying impulse transfer. After collision both bodies should visibly wobble and settle based on their parameter values. Add a Reset button that returns both balls to starting positions and zeroes velocities. Add a Gravity Toggle button that switches between zero-gravity and downward gravity (0, -9.8, 0), causing both bodies to sag under their own weight. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 2, 10) with OrbitControls. Use a neutral HDR-style lighting rig: one DirectionalLight from upper-right, one HemisphereLight for ambient fill, and a subtle ground plane with shadow receiving. Render at window resolution with antialiasing and toneMapping set to ACESFilmicToneMapping. The simulation loop must run at fixed 60Hz substeps inside requestAnimationFrame. Ensure all six slider changes, the drag-launch, the reset, and the gravity toggle each produce a validated visible effect, totaling at least eight distinct interaction steps.
